antigravity.point_of_view: Antigravity CLI is the supported Google terminal-agent path for individual Gemini CLI migration. It exposes print mode, model listing, plugin management, and prompt execution through agy.

skills.description: Manage Antigravity plugins that package skills and workflows.
skills.name: plugin-management

skills.description: Route terminal prompts across 11 available models.
skills.name: model-routing

skills.description: Run noninteractive terminal-agent prompts with bounded print timeouts.
skills.name: headless-print-mode

gemini.point_of_view: Gemini CLI is the terminal agent reached through @google/gemini-cli. It exposes command-managed skills with SKILL.md packages, optional scripts/references/assets, MCP listings, extensions, and headless prompts.

jules.point_of_view: Jules is the asynchronous coding/workflow agent reached through the bridge. Its local project skill system lives in .agents/skills and its operational contract is loaded from .agents/AGENTS.md, AKC, gotchas, and memory.

skills.description: Run before starting any complex feature, new module, or major change. Reads the project context files, interviews the user one question at a time to resolve design decisions, and produces a clear, structured implementation plan.
skills.name: architect

skills.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
skills.name: diagnosing-bugs

skills.description: >- Boots Jules Bridge, Jules CLI, and ngrok always-on remote access on Windows without admin (guest-safe). Restores auth, registers logon startup, keeps PC online with monitor off. Use when the user says /god, god mode, boot bridge, always-on backdoor, black screen boot, or Jules Bridge startup on the 64GB RAM PC.
skills.name: god

skills.description: Interview the user relentlessly to reach a shared design concept before any planning or coding begins. Use this at the very start of any new feature, project, or non-trivial task. Prevents misalignment. Never eagerly jump to producing a plan — keep asking until full alignment is achieved.
skills.name: grill-me

skills.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.
skills.name: grill-with-docs

skills.description: Run after creating or modifying API routes or module layouts. Captures coding patterns, route structures, and middleware registration to maintain system-wide consistency.
skills.name: imprint

skills.description: Identify shallow modules in a codebase and refactor them into deep modules (from John Ousterhout's "A Philosophy of Software Design"). Use when the AI keeps getting confused navigating the codebase, tests are hard to write, or you feel cognitive overload from too many small files with tangled concerns. Produces a clean module boundary map and executes the refactor incrementally.
skills.name: improve-codebase-architecture

skills.description: Break a PRD into independently grabbable implementation tickets using vertical slices (tracer bullets). Creates a kanban board of issues with dependency/blocking relationships and AFK vs human-in-loop classification. CRITICAL: Issues must be vertical slices, NOT horizontal layers.
skills.name: prd-to-issues

skills.description: Implements a Ralph Loop — a self-correcting, ticket-driven agentic loop that picks the next most important ticket, implements it with TDD principles, commits, and repeats. Named after Ralph Wiggum (The Simpsons) who just keeps trying the same thing until it works. Run this skill when you want to autonomously work through a backlog of tickets in doc/tickets/.
skills.name: ralph-loop

skills.description: Run when a session is stuck, tests are failing repeatedly, or the agent is in a doom loop. Diagnoses the current failure mode and provides the correct remediation steps.
skills.name: recover

skills.description: Run at the end of every coding session. Synthesizes decisions made, patterns established, and progress completed during the session, and compresses them into a memory file in the `memory/` directory.
skills.name: remember

skills.description: Run after completing any feature or file modification. Checks the implementation against the plan, verifies code standards, and surfaces potential bugs.
skills.name: review

skills.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
skills.name: tdd

skills.description: Scan the codebase to extract domain terminology and create a Ubiquitous Language document (from Domain-Driven Design). Use this to reduce AI verbosity, improve alignment between planning and implementation, and give the AI a shared vocabulary with the codebase. Run this at the start of any project or when the AI seems to be "talking across purposes".
skills.name: ubiquitous-language

skills.description: Distill the current conversation (ideally a completed grill-me session) into a Product Requirements Document. The PRD is the "destination document" — it defines WHERE you're going, not HOW you'll get there. Use after a grill-me session, or with a detailed problem description as input.
skills.name: write-prd
